definition: Humility is a relatively deep-seated emotional attitude or habit of mind in which a person places themselves low in worth, character, or achievement, especially in relation to moral or religious standards. In this historical account, it is presented as more rooted in temperament and less tied to comparison with other people than modesty.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Humility; pinned source text

reasons: “worth” is not supported by the source text, which says only that humility is a disposition to rank oneself low in character and achievements.
The definition should stay closer to the historical wording; the source does not frame humility as low self-worth in general.

The definition claims humility is “less tied to comparison with other people than modesty,” but the packet only says it has “less reference to other persons” than modesty; “comparison” is not explicitly supported.
The definition includes “low in worth” (in addition to “character, or achievement”); the packet specifies “rank oneself low in character and achievements,” but does not use the term “worth.”
